_note: Draft EDOP signature schema — April 2026. Dummy instance for Ur (30.9626N, 46.1033E). Values are illustrative; some approximate from prior analysis. Fields marked [*] not yet implemented.

period._note: D band suppressed for pre-industrial period. Temporal datasets queried where available.

A_physiographic._note: Bedrock physical character; stable over geological timescales

B_hydroclimatic._note: s = local sub-basin; near_u = decay-weighted near-upstream aggregate [*]; u = full upstream catchment

C_bioclimatic._note: Proxies for ecological and land-surface conditions

D_anthropocene._note: Modern-era markers; suppress or qualify for pre-industrial analysis

divergence._note: s/u ratio per variable; values > 1 indicate drier/warmer/etc. locally than upstream

scale_sensitivity._note: How much the local (s) signature changes between basin levels [*]

temporal._note: Period-specific climate context from LMR v2.1 (Tardif et al. 2019). Gridded reanalysis, 2°×2°, 20-member MC ensemble. Values are actual extractions for Ur (30.0N, 46.0E), 0–100 CE.
temporal.source: Last Millennium Reanalysis v2.1 (Tardif et al. 2019)

pdsi._note: Palmer Drought Severity Index; 0 = climatological mean, negative = drier, positive = wetter
pdsi._interpretation: Near-climatological mean throughout, with exceptionally low variability (std 0.040). All decadal means cluster within ±0.05 of zero — no sustained drought or wet anomaly for the entire century. Ur was already long past its peak by 0 CE; the climate signal offers no forcing explanation for its earlier decline.

air_temperature._note: [*] Surface air temperature anomaly relative to 1961–1990 baseline; °C — not yet extracted

precipitation._note: [*] Precipitation rate (prate); kg/m²/s — not yet extracted

sst._note: Sea surface temperature — not applicable for inland location

volcanic._note: Event annotation from eVolv2k v4 (Sigl & Toohey 2024). 50-year context window: -50 to 100 CE.
volcanic._interpretation: The dominant feature is Okmok II (43 BCE, 48 Tg), one of the largest eruptions in the full eVolv2k catalog, with strong Northern Hemisphere loading (asymmetry 0.87). McConnell et al. (2020, PNAS) link this event to climate and agricultural disruption in the late Roman Republic. Within the 0–100 CE period itself, volcanic activity is modest — most events are small and Southern Hemisphere-dominant (asymmetry 0.00), indicating minimal stratospheric loading over Mesopotamia. The century is volcanically quiet by the standards of the broader catalog.

coverage._note: Documents data sources and temporal basis for each signature component. Never omitted; fields are null when not yet implemented.

dendrochronology.source: PAGES 2k v2.0.0 — point records only, not yet integrated

narrative: [*] Ur occupies a hyper-arid local environment (aridity index 5, 94mm/yr precipitation) fed by an upstream catchment receiving over four times the local rainfall — a sharp local/upstream divergence characteristic of alluvial civilizations dependent on distant water sources. The site lies approximately 890km upstream from the Persian Gulf, close enough for maritime access while insulated from direct tidal influence. Terrestrial conditions alone would predict marginal viability; the combination of upstream water delivery and downstream sea access explains the site's historical centrality. In the first century CE, when Ur was already in long decline, LMR climate data shows near-climatological mean moisture conditions with unusually low variability — no climate forcing to explain the site's trajectory in either direction. The major volcanic event of the period (Okmok II, 43 BCE, 48 Tg) falls just before the query window and was Northern Hemisphere-dominant; the century itself is volcanically quiet.
